source: SALARY_CALCULATOR_SPEC.md §6 — 2026 Continente brackets (rendimento coletável, rate, parcela a abater). Note: a cut to these rates, backdated to all of 2026, was approved by the Council of Ministers on 17 Sept 2026 and is pending Parliament as of the spec's writing — a 2026-rev2 rule set slot should be added once published. VERIFY against Lei n.º 73-A/2025 (OE 2026) / CIRS art. 68.º before this ships to real users.

solidarityRate.note: taxa adicional de solidariedade on rendimento coletável above 80,000 (2.5%) and above 250,000 (an additional 2.5%, i.e. 5% total) — Continente/Madeira. CONFIRMED (not just the spec's own figure) via a live lookup of art. 68.º-A CIRS commentary: Açores uses 1.75%/3.5% on the same thresholds — matches the spec exactly. Açores' own irs-brackets rule file (Phase 2) should use those rates.

deductions.note: Dependent figures taken from SALARY_CALCULATOR_SPEC.md §6 deduções à coleta (v1 subset). The two disability figures are CONFIRMED directly against the primary legal text (art. 87.º CIRS, fetched live from Portal das Finanças), which corrects a misreading of the spec: disabilityTaxpayer (4× IAS = 2,148.52) applies to ANY taxpayer with a qualifying disability regardless of marital status — the spec's own phrasing ('per non-married taxpayer') was imprecise, not the article itself; disabilityDependent (2.5× IAS = 1,342.83) applies per dependent OR ascendant with disability (this engine has no ascendants field, so only the dependent case is implemented). mínimo de existência (2026 reference €12,880/year, confirmed = max(12,880, 1.5×14×IAS) per art. 70.º CIRS) is implemented only for the simple case (full exemption at/below that gross-income threshold) — the sliding-taper formula between ~€12,880 and ~€14,641 is real but genuinely complex (art. 70.º §2 b/c) and not confidently enough sourced here to implement without a known-good test case to verify against; left unimplemented rather than guessed. VERIFY every value here against CIRS before this ships to real users.
